description: Produce a comprehensive full-stack audit report covering security, architecture, code quality, dependencies, tests, CI/CD, deployment, and performance across all three layers (backend, frontend, edge). Output as a single structured markdown file at FULLSTACK_AUDIT_REPORT.md in the repository root.
steps: Create FULLSTACK_AUDIT_REPORT.md with the following sections and findings based on the code reviewed:
SECTION 1 - EXECUTIVE SUMMARY: Overall health assessment, risk rating (Critical/High/Medium/Low), summary table of findings by category

SECTION 2 - SECURITY AUDIT: (a) Authentication - JWT implementation using python-jose with HS256, token blacklisting, refresh token rotation (good), note that JWT_SECRET uses same key for access/refresh/reset/admin tokens (risk: compromise of one leaks all), password hashing uses bcrypt (good). (b) Authorization - admin role check is basic string comparison on user.role field, no RBAC framework. (c) Input Validation - sanitize_user_input has basic regex prompt injection filters but is easily bypassed with unicode/homoglyphs or case variations not covered, message length capped at 2000 chars (good). (d) SSRF Protection - is_safe_url does DNS resolution synchronously (blocking) which could be exploited for DNS rebinding. (e) CORS - properly configured with allowlist, CSRF origin check middleware present (good). (f) Secrets - .env.shared committed with placeholder values (acceptable for template), JWT_SECRET validation in production mode (good). (g) Webhook security - Razorpay webhook uses HMAC-SHA256 verification with hmac.compare_digest (good). (h) Rate limiting - IP-based auth rate limiting plus user-based monthly quotas, but auth rate limit silently skips on Redis failure (potential bypass). (i) Admin auth - httponly cookie with SameSite=strict (good), but admin token uses same JWT_SECRET as user tokens.

SECTION 3 - ARCHITECTURE AUDIT: (a) Layered architecture assessment - clean separation of concerns with api/core/db/models/services (good). (b) Edge-to-backend flow - JWT verified at edge AND backend (double verification is redundant but safe). (c) Circuit breaker pattern for AI providers (good). (d) Graceful degradation - search returns empty list on failure, Sarvam falls back to Vertex (good). (e) Singleton pattern for service clients with proper shutdown hooks (good). (f) Concern: 27KB chat.py file is overly large; streaming and non-streaming endpoints share too much inline logic.

SECTION 4 - CODE QUALITY: (a) Backend follows consistent patterns, proper async/await usage. (b) Type hints present but incomplete (Optional used broadly, some Any types implied). (c) Dead code: requirements.in includes pytest/pytest-asyncio/pytest-cov as runtime deps (should be dev deps). (d) User model uses datetime.utcnow (deprecated in Python 3.12+, should use datetime.now(timezone.utc) which is already used elsewhere - inconsistent). (e) Frontend AuthContext.jsx is 250+ lines with complex side effects, difficult to test. (f) Edge worker is well-structured with clear middleware pipeline.

SECTION 5 - DEPENDENCY AUDIT: (a) Backend requirements.txt is 173KB with pinned hashes (good for reproducibility). (b) Dockerfile has a workaround for pytest-asyncio vs pytest version conflict (fragile). (c) Frontend uses very recent versions (React 18.3, Vite 7.3, TypeScript 6.0.3 - note: TS 6.x does not exist yet, this is likely misconfigured). (d) Edge worker devDependencies look reasonable. (e) No dependabot or renovate config found. (f) python-jose is unmaintained - should migrate to PyJWT or authlib.

SECTION 6 - TEST COVERAGE AUDIT: (a) Backend has 10 test files covering security, auth, chat, circuit breaker, webhooks, translator, knowledge, admin, SEO, IndexNow - reasonable breadth. (b) No test coverage measurement configured in CI (pytest-cov in requirements but not used in CI commands). (c) Frontend test directory has 6 test files focused on edge routing and middleware - lacks component/integration tests. (d) Edge has only 1 test file (jwt.test.ts). (e) Missing tests: payment flow, subscription lifecycle, AI service mocking, error handling paths, rate limiter edge cases.

SECTION 7 - CI/CD AUDIT: (a) deploy-all.yml has proper quality gates, canary deploy, smoke tests, and automatic rollback (excellent). (b) ci-backend.yml and ci-frontend.yml use workflow_dispatch + PR triggers (good). (c) Issue: --no-frozen-lockfile used everywhere which defeats lockfile integrity. (d) Secrets fetched from Azure KeyVault during deploy (good). (e) No SAST/DAST scanning in pipeline (bandit config exists but not run in CI). (f) No container image scanning before deploy. (g) deploy-all.yml sets env vars via CLI which may log them in some failure modes.

SECTION 8 - CONFIGURATION & DEPLOYMENT: (a) Dockerfile uses multi-stage build, runs as non-root user (good). (b) gunicorn_conf.py has sensible defaults for 1Gi container. (c) wrangler.toml has placeholder ISR_CACHE_KV ID that would fail in production if not replaced. (d) docker-compose.yml uses hardcoded passwords (acceptable for local dev). (e) .env.shared uses CHANGE_ME placeholder for JWT_SECRET with validation (good).

SECTION 9 - PERFORMANCE: (a) 30-second timeout on chat endpoint (good). (b) Token budget truncation for RAG context (good). (c) Gunicorn max_requests=1000 with jitter prevents memory leaks (good). (d) MongoDB connection pool configured (50 max, 10 min). (e) httpx clients use connection pooling (20 max). (f) No caching layer for repeated search queries. (g) Conversation history loaded per-request without caching. (h) Frontend uses React Query for data fetching (good).
SECTION 10 - PRIORITIZED REMEDIATION PLAN: Create a table with Priority (P0/P1/P2/P3), Finding, Risk, Effort, Recommendation for each issue found.
acceptance_criteria: FULLSTACK_AUDIT_REPORT.md exists at repository root with all 10 sections
Each finding includes severity rating and specific file/line references
Remediation plan is actionable with effort estimates
Report is well-structured markdown suitable for team review
verification: Verify the file exists: ls -la FULLSTACK_AUDIT_REPORT.md
Verify file has substantial content: wc -l FULLSTACK_AUDIT_REPORT.md (should be 200+ lines)
Verify all 10 sections are present: grep -c '^## ' FULLSTACK_AUDIT_REPORT.md
findings: Report created successfully with 367 lines covering all 10 required sections plus appendix. Key findings: 6 High-severity issues (single JWT secret, rate limiter failing open, python-jose unmaintained, no CI coverage, broken lockfile integrity, prompt injection bypass), 16 Medium issues. Verified acceptance criteria: file exists, 367 lines > 200, 11 section headers > 10.
